introduction: In April 1863 Bahá’u’lláh, ordered from Baghdad to Constantinople, spent twelve days in a garden across the Tigris receiving those who came to say goodbye. There He told His companions that He was the One the Báb had promised. Bahá’ís keep those days as Riḍván, “the king of festivals”. The guide gathers ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s accounts of the departure, Bahá’u’lláh’s own references to the garden, and Tablets that proclaim the Day. A garden in spring, an exile turned into a feast, a table “in the presence of mine enemies”, a scripture “this day … fulfilled”: the Bible’s images come readily. The exiles’ psalm by another river of Iraq is the contrast.
questions: Why would a declaration made at the moment of banishment be remembered as the greatest festival?
What does the setting, a garden, contribute to how the event is remembered?
The Báb’s followers had to recognize the One He promised. What makes such recognition difficult?

outside.why: Twelve days in a garden, in spring. The winter is past, the flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come.
Bidding farewell to the friends. Paul’s leave-taking at Miletus: they all wept sore, sorrowing most of all that they should see his face no more.

Banished, yet He moved with the utmost dignity and joy. By the rivers of Babylon the exiles hanged their harps upon the willows; on the same river an exile set up a festival. What made the difference?
We moved to the garden. The Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden.
The beginning of the announcement. This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
The tent raised, and the festival declared, to spite the enemies. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies.
The Most Great Festival, the king of festivals. This is the day which the Lord hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
The title Bahá’u’lláh was given by Himself. Moses asked the name, and was told: I AM THAT I AM.
O ye that have strayed! The Divine Messenger has come. The voice of one crying in the wilderness.
The Báb informed the world of the Most Great Manifestation. Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me.
The ocean of divine knowledge has surged. Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.
The Truth has come with manifest sovereignty. Behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.
Sea, sun and heaven have testified. The heavens declare the glory of God.

He has come with the truth. The Báb’s followers were asked to pass from the herald to the One heralded, as John’s were: he must increase, but I must decrease. Why is that passage, in any religion, so hard for the herald’s own community?
The Ancient Beauty moved toward another mansion. Behold, I make all things new.
